text:
Carter Verhaeghe has three Stanley Cup rings and 21 points in 24 games, and on the surface this is the same reliable Panther who scores when it counts. Ten goals, eight power-play points, a nightly 18 minutes in the top six.

Look underneath and the season has been kinder to him than his play. Florida has scored 11.1 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, the biggest cushion we flag on anyone in this group, and at 5v5 the Panthers are roughly even on expected goals with him out there (about 50%), a little worse than without him. He's also shooting 19% against a likely range of 12 to 17%.

His own game is fine. The last ten games brought nine points, seven of them assists, which fits what Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking said about him last season: 93rd percentile among forwards in primary shot assists, with 72% of his exits leaving the zone with the puck. Evolving-Hockey had him facing 94th-percentile competition. Expect the points to cool toward his true rate of about 2.5 per 60 even if nothing about how he plays changes.
